The coadministration of cobicistat with strong CYP3A inducers may lead to reduced plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, potentially resulting in a loss of therapeutic efficacy and the development of resistance. Avoid such combinations or consider alternative drugs. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (intranasal) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and doxorubicin liposomal by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustments may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg orally once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 6. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug, as coadministration may result in a loss of therapeutic efficacy and resistance development. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of elbasvir/grazoprevir with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating medications for stem cell mobilization, during the duration of these medications, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 10. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by mechanisms involving OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eszopiclone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Consider nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (transdermal and transmucosal) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 22. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fidaxomicin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat and elvitegravir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Elvitegravir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose as needed. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor for QTc prolongation if coadministration is necessary. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivosedinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosedinib dose to 250 mg daily. Resume the recommended dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 37. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, administer 500 mg lapatinib daily and adjust the dose after discontinuing cobicistat. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 42. Lenolisib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lenolisib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
